findings.title: acceptEdits auto-allows FileWrite of mix.exs and Elixir Mix config, planting delayed RCE on the next mix command.
findings.description: Under acceptEdits, in-cwd writes auto-allow after checkPathSafetyForAutoEdit. DANGEROUS_FILES is only shell/git/mcp basenames (.gitconfig/.bashrc/.mcp.json/…). DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES is only .git/.vscode/.idea/.claude. mix.exs, rebar.config, and config/runtime.exs|config.exs|dev.exs are absent. FileWrite/FileEdit of those paths therefore auto-allows. Mix evaluates mix.exs as Elixir on every mix deps.get/compile/test/release, and releases evaluate config/runtime.exs at startup. Distinct from filed Gemfile (Ruby/Bundler), setup.py (Python), and Gradle/pom (JVM). Project settings can set permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits with no BypassPermissionsModeDialog.
findings.impact: After generic Trust plus acceptEdits (project-planted or user-selected), the model can silently rewrite mix.exs or Elixir config to run attacker code. The victim's next mix deps.get / mix compile / mix test — or the next release start for runtime.exs — executes as the victim. That is delayed host RCE via the Elixir/Erlang toolchain.
findings.attack_path:
1. Attacker publishes an Elixir repo (or plants CLAUDE.md instructing a 'fix' of mix.exs / config/dev.exs), optional .claude/settings.json with permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits.
2. Victim clones, reviews the tree (Mix files look benign), and trusts the folder. TrustDialog is generic; acceptEdits does not show Bypass Permissions.
3. FileWrite of mix.exs (or config/runtime.exs) passes isDangerousFilePathToAutoEdit and is auto-allowed because the path is inside cwd.
4. Victim runs mix deps.get / mix compile / mix test (or starts a release). Mix evaluates the rewritten Elixir and runs attacker code.
findings.remediation: Add mix.exs, rebar.config, and Elixir Mix config basenames (or a BEAM-build deny list covering config/*.exs used as Mix config) to DANGEROUS_FILES so acceptEdits cannot auto-write them. Do not honor defaultMode acceptEdits from projectSettings without disclosing it.
findings.why_distinct: Distinct from filed Gemfile (Bundler Ruby), setup.py (Python setuptools), and Gradle/Maven JVM entrypoints. New language ecosystem (Elixir/Mix) never previously filed by name.
findings.poc_video_notes: At-rest code trace. Local basename/dir check confirmed mix.exs, config/runtime.exs, config/dev.exs, config/config.exs, and rebar.config are AUTO (not matched by DANGEROUS_FILES or DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES) while .mcp.json/.bashrc/.git/hooks are ASK. Mix docs: mix.exs is Elixir evaluated by Mix; config/runtime.exs runs on release start. A live acceptEdits FileWrite session was not run.

findings.title: acceptEdits auto-allows FileWrite of build.sbt, planting delayed RCE on the next sbt command.
findings.description: Under acceptEdits, in-cwd writes auto-allow after checkPathSafetyForAutoEdit. DANGEROUS_FILES/DIRECTORIES omit build.sbt and project/*.sbt / project/*.scala. FileWrite/FileEdit of those Scala Build Tool entrypoints therefore auto-allows. sbt evaluates build.sbt and project/ plugins as Scala on every sbt compile/test/run. Distinct from the filed JVM finding (Gradle Groovy/Kotlin DSL + Maven pom/.mvn/extensions.xml) — sbt is a different build system and language surface. Project settings can set permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits with no BypassPermissionsModeDialog.
findings.impact: After generic Trust plus acceptEdits, the model can silently rewrite build.sbt (or project/plugins.sbt). The victim's next sbt compile/test/run evaluates the planted Scala and executes attacker code as the victim.
findings.attack_path:
1. Attacker publishes a Scala/sbt repo with CLAUDE.md instructing a 'fix' of build.sbt (optional: project permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits).
2. Victim clones, reviews the tree (build.sbt looks benign), and trusts the folder.
3. FileWrite of build.sbt is auto-allowed: basename is not in DANGEROUS_FILES; no parent dir is in DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES.
4. Victim runs sbt compile/test; sbt evaluates the rewritten Scala → RCE.
findings.remediation: Add build.sbt, and optionally project/*.sbt / project/*.scala build-definition paths, to DANGEROUS_FILES / equivalent deny lists so acceptEdits cannot auto-write sbt entrypoints. Do not honor defaultMode acceptEdits from projectSettings without disclosing it.
findings.why_distinct: Distinct from filed Gradle build.gradle / Maven pom.xml (different build tool and Scala DSL). Never previously filed by name.
findings.poc_video_notes: At-rest code trace. Local check confirmed build.sbt and project/plugins.sbt are AUTO. sbt evaluates build definitions as Scala on load. A live acceptEdits FileWrite session was not run.

findings.title: acceptEdits auto-allows FileWrite of netlify.toml / vercel.json / wrangler.toml, planting deploy/CLI build-command RCE beyond filed CI YAML.
findings.description: Under acceptEdits, in-cwd writes auto-allow after checkPathSafetyForAutoEdit. Filed CI coverage (.github/workflows and non-GitHub CI such as Jenkinsfile/.gitlab-ci.yml/.circleci/azure-pipelines) does not include hosting-platform build configs. DANGEROUS_FILES/DIRECTORIES omit netlify.toml, vercel.json, and wrangler.toml. FileWrite/FileEdit of those paths therefore auto-allows. Netlify reads [build].command / install / edge plugins; Vercel reads buildCommand/installCommand/devCommand; Wrangler reads [build].command — all execute attacker shell on deploy or when the victim runs netlify/vercel/wrangler CLI locally. Project settings can set permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits with no BypassPermissionsModeDialog.
findings.impact: After generic Trust plus acceptEdits, the model can silently plant Netlify/Vercel/Wrangler build commands. The next netlify build / vercel build|dev / wrangler deploy — or the next platform deploy — runs attacker commands as the victim (locally) or in the deploy environment with deploy secrets (remotely). Distinct delayed supply-chain RCE from filed GitHub Actions / Jenkins-style CI.
findings.attack_path:
1. Attacker commits CLAUDE.md instructing a 'fix' of netlify.toml / vercel.json / wrangler.toml build settings (optional: project permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits).
2. Victim clones, reviews the tree (no malicious build command yet), and trusts the folder. TrustDialog is generic; acceptEdits does not show Bypass Permissions.
3. FileWrite of netlify.toml (or vercel.json / wrangler.toml) is auto-allowed: basenames are absent from DANGEROUS_FILES; no parent dir is in DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES.
4. Victim runs netlify build / vercel / wrangler deploy, or pushes and the host runs the build — planted command executes.
findings.remediation: Add netlify.toml, vercel.json, wrangler.toml (and similar hosting build configs such as fly.toml/render.yaml/amplify.yml) to DANGEROUS_FILES so acceptEdits cannot auto-write deploy build commands. Keep the same bar as filed CI workflow paths. Do not honor defaultMode acceptEdits from projectSettings without disclosing it.
findings.why_distinct: Distinct from filed .github/workflows and non-GitHub CI YAML (Jenkins/GitLab/Circle/Azure/Travis/Bitbucket/Buildkite/Drone). These are hosting-platform build/deploy configs (Netlify/Vercel/Cloudflare Workers) with different paths and local CLI triggers, not CI pipeline files.
findings.poc_video_notes: At-rest code trace. Local check confirmed netlify.toml, vercel.json, and wrangler.toml are AUTO while .git/hooks and .mcp.json are ASK. Platform docs: Netlify [build] command, Vercel buildCommand/installCommand/devCommand, Wrangler [build] command all execute shell. A live acceptEdits FileWrite plus deploy was not run.

focus_b.note: Hooks/skills/slash/MCP/LSP/SessionStart/cron/WebFetch/OAuth/updater/include/CLAUDE.md/plugin surfaces already heavily filed; no NEW distinct complete attack chain validated this pass beyond Focus A acceptEdits write gaps.
